hints.content:
Let's examine the rotation of a single point, such as point $C$. This will tell us the angle of rotation, since all points undergo the same transformation.

Imagine a circle that passes through point $C$ with a center at point $Q$.  What portion of the circle do we rotate through to reach the image? In which direction?

We need to rotate point $C$ through about $\dfrac{5}{12}$ of the circle to reach the image $C'$, so that is about $150^\circ$. 

![](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/82273f211882e88d6f5e0f7e307b7fb971802fc2)

Since we rotate *clockwise*, the angle of rotation is *negative*. That means point $C$ has an angle of rotation of $-150^\circ$.
The angle of rotation for quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $-150^\circ$.
